Title: 마른 가지에 바람처럼 7 (Like Wind on a Dry Branch, Vol. 7)
Author: Dalsaeowl
My Review:
Vol. 7
Episode 72 ~ 83

I can’t say this is my favorite volume but I do love the way the author intentionally juxtaposes specific scenes or moments to its exact counterpart to really drive home a message for the readers.

For example: A mother carrying for its child and child caring for its mother is very reasonable idea to grasp.

Now pairing this idea to making a choice between saving mother or child is a much more complex situation..

On one side we have Rieta a mother who’s lost her child and can’t live without the grief of her family circumstances bearing down on her. She without hesitation would chose the child live rather than the mother. She herself living with the loss of her baby makes her feel guilty for continuing to live without her child..

One the other hand we have Killian who had his mother killed twice and who do anything in his power to save her. He chooses the mother.

We eventually find out it’s actually a father saving his child but I digress the idea still stands and honestly it makes it even better. I love that this WEBTOON does not shy away from portraying such deep values emotions and concepts.

Title: A Court of Thorns and Roses (A Court of Thorns and Roses, #1)
Author: Sarah J. Maas
My Review:
A Court of Thorns and Roses tested my patience more than once. I liked it — but just barely. The Stockholm syndrome undertone was loud and persistent, and honestly, it wore me down.

Lucien and Rhysand completely stole the show. By the end, they outshined Tamlin by a mile. Tamlin’s silence “for her sake” was… fine, I guess. But then he turns around and puts her in danger in one reckless moment? Wildly unattractive. I lost all respect for him then and there. Rhysand was by far way more deserving of praise than he received by putting his neck on the line for her and others several times. Though to be completely clear he has no damn concept of consent and is willing to humiliate Feyre at any time and will torture and torment anyone insignificant to him. Soo yeah no man in this book is fantastic, outstanding or exceptional on any count.

Feyre being illiterate made every scene involving written words agonizing. With all that downtime, she still couldn’t pick up reading or writing at a reasonable pace. Watching her struggle was like dragging a boulder uphill — frustrating and slow.

Nesta, though, redeemed the book halfway through. She was a breath of fresh air: sharp, assertive, and unapologetic. I understood her coldness toward her family — she resisted the system in her own way, and her complexity and stubbornness made her compelling. The sisterly bonding moments were among the most heartfelt in the book.

The father, on the other hand, could kick rocks. His last-minute vanishing act during Feyre’s farewell summed up his character: passive, cowardly, and absent. He never stepped up for his family, never took true accountability, and never showed any real growth or remorse. Makes my mouth taste bitter thinking about how he told feyre to go to her death at the start was honestly just for his sake in the end despite relying on her skills and trade heavily..

Overall, it was an ok read — boosted a lot by TikTok hype — but it’s definitely not for everyone.

Title: The Book of Doors
Author: Gareth  Brown
My Review:
I’m still not sure how to put my shock and delight into words when it comes to The Book of Doors. It’s not a cozy romance, and it’s not bone-chilling horror—it sits somewhere in between, constantly defying expectations. The story doesn’t even unfold in order most of the time, yet I could easily read it again and still gasp audibly at the plot twists that drop every few chapters.

The villains are truly vile—evil in a way that makes your skin crawl—while the good characters are like the soothing relief of ice water on a sweltering day. The concept is a mind-bender, often posing impossible questions without clear answers. I felt genuine rage when the wicked walked free and frustration when the good paid the price.

And that ending? It tied the whole story together in a perfect loop, like a song you can’t help but replay. A fascinating, unpredictable read that lingers long after you close the book.

I graduated from college recently with computer engineering and just felt lost. My favorite and most hated places in the world were no longer in my daily life. My favorite people I’d no longer see daily. My dorm life suddenly ended and so did the classes I had earnestly attended and enjoyed(and hated). I came back home to a house I hadn’t lived in any longer than for some weeks during the summer (I still get the light switches wrong). I felt quite out of place and I needed to get out. I took my kindle to the local library and enjoyed the environment which felt closest to my usual life before graduation. I adored this book and I fell in love with myself again after it. I’m stepping into 2025 feeling a bit better without anxiety.

I fell in love with all the characters good and bad; I won't lie I thought the cat's backstories were more heartfelt than the mayor's to an extent. He was a necessary death, but it still broke my heart to have needed it to resolve his one wish of getting Su-ha better again. He promised that much to his sister years before and he was able to do just that by dying to protect Su-ha. Dongbae got his girl at last too, just needed to do what was right first. He was a good friend and Jeongwha would be proud. That scumbag of a birth father Su-ha had if he had a Zuko arc i might have flipped. He came back to Su-ha only for money so I'm glad he's dead. It's unfortunate that his death caused the downfall all of Jeonghwa's efforts (on surface value) making it known there's a zombie in the area. Author: Marissa Meyer
My Review: Cinder is a cyborg. The setting is Asian. There are conflicts that have lasted decades between two peoples Lunar and Earthen. To settle the impending war, the Lunar Empress requires marriage to the Emperor of the Eastern Commonwealth (once current-day Beijing). Though the strange mesh of ideas clashes together, it was an enjoyable read. I liked the retelling of a classic cinderella with such brazen twists like this. It was a fresh take on the topic of part human - part robot discussion. Though I did want to know more about her being "inhumane" as she felt really human-like to me as I read. I was not off-put by the lack of her tears or blushing as much as the wrenching of her wires in her legs as she replaced her foot. I wish we got to see more of that robotic tendency or lack of emotions like love that everyone was fast to hate/despise/ and belittle. People were quick on degrading cyborgs(once human before an accident) from the status of human to someone worth throwing away as a test subject. So I'm curious why it really got so bad in such prejudices. I'll be reading more of the series but this was a good stepping point into a new world open to many new ideas and interesting twists on the classics.

Title: The Sword of Summer (Magnus Chase and the Gods of Asgard, #1)
Author: Rick Riordan
My Review:
The Sword of Summer, Sumarbrander, is a talking sword. Its sole purpose is to kill its' former owner and the only ones capable of owning the weapon are anyone from the Frey descendants. That list is short with only Magnus Chase on it. However, the sword is still destined to be stolen from him at some point to start Ragnarok.

I did like the ending but the journey in between was just very repetitive in a way. There's a problem then it's given a partial solution, then another problem that leads to yet another partial solution. Finally when it looks like there's a definitive solution we are all back at the start with little to no change.

Though I did like the characters and all the gods and how they all acted/interacted, they all were not that memorable. I seriously hated Jack (Sumarbrander's "new" name) throughout the majority of the book. As helpful as he was, he did get on my nerves a bit with his commentary and lack of guidance (?) in the journey. Loki on the other hand was somehow very much intriguing. He had my heartstrings for a moment just talking about his past and how his punishment came to be. He's charming in a dangerous sort of way. Too bad he's still a villain.

It was still very easy to read and comprehend without much trouble outside of just being unable to pronounce Norse words (but that's a personal problem). I do love the lore and all the new worlds that open up to us readers. But it can get a bit complicated to keep up in terms of where they are in the journey through the worlds and on the quest all at once. I'll probably pick up the next book to see how it goes but I'll have to do that sooner than later if I don't want to forget all that's happened already.

Title: I'll Save this Damned Family!
Author: Munirang
My Review:
Currently, 1-81 are completed! This webtoon is on hiatus at the moment.

Tara Elias is such a wonderfully built character. She starts off with a plan and sticks to it. She grows with every challenge that comes her way and tackles it head-on, unlike other female leads that whine. She isn't the type to wait around for someone to save her so best believe she's capable of saving herself and those she cares for. And even when she is not yet skillful enough to handle the situation, she has the determination to learn how to approach situations like that better for the next time. Her power is in having the ability to adapt and learn for the better.

I don't particularly like the main male lead but he isn't as bad as I thought initially. Bad meaning, unlikeable not like he had any unforgivable faults.

I can't wait to see where this is going as of currently the opening scene hasn't played out yet. Additionally, I'd like to mention how much I love how the author depicts the change in Tara's appearance slowly. It's not abrupt and the amount of work she puts into changing her physique is admirable and inspiring. She works out and slowly starts to change her unhealthy diet and I respect the author for not glazing over how Tara lost weight.

Title: Spy x Family, Vol. 1
Author: Tatsuya Endo
Additional Authors: Casey Loe, Rina Mapa, Jimmy Presler
My Review:
My only regret is not picking this up sooner. I fell in love with Anya, Loid and Yor on the big screens and I just needed more. (The anime is worth the weekly wait for new episodes, I highly recommend it.)

Volume 1 is consistent of Missions 1-5.

To put into perspective of the plot there is an ongoing cold war between two countries Westalis(west) and Ostana(east). The opening of the manga is a diplomat from the western country is having his driver take him to the embassy quickly only to discover the brakes failed and they crash. Westalis intelligence view this as Ostana sparking conflict. Westalis place the operation to prevent war from erupting in the hands of their most capable spy, Twilight.

Twilight, Loid (fake name), is given Operation Strix which entails him making a family and having his child enroll in a prestigious school for elites of society, Eden College. There he is tasked with keeping tabs on Ostana's elites particularly Donovan Desmond, the leader of a political power group in Ostana.

His first objective is to adopt a child with enough intellect to enroll at Eden College. This leads him to start his search in a pretty dingy part of town in a run-down orphanage. It's safe to say kids from this place had shady and rough childhoods and Anya is no exception. She is one of those characters that are just so charming. She is in fact a telepath and her ability to read minds is amazing, but her own mental capabilities handicap her powers. Just imagine how overpowered mindreading can possibly be with a spy father by your side as you infiltrate a school of prestigious rich kids whose parents own massive brands or are part of secret organizations and are government authorities. Just imagine that, but now picture that power is in the hands of a child whose intelligence is not enough to actually use her powers to their true potential.

Anya is my favorite because believable her child characteristic is portrayed. She's absolutely lovable and stupidly endearing. I love her dearly and her faces are just amazing to watch.

Yor is the mother of the family. She, unbeknownst to Loid, is an assassin for hire in Ostana. Even with her shocking occupation, she dreams of romance and sweet life with a loving family. Loid and Anya are that for her and I just crave this relationship. Though built on deception (Loid for his mission and Yor to ease her brother's worries), the memorable moments that follow after through making this fake family will always have a place in my heart. Yor's kindness hasn't diminished regardless of her job and upbringing but only increased it looks like. Her connection to Anya almost immediately is so heartwarming and I do wish all the happiness for them all.

Please watch or read this if you haven't picked it up. You'll only regret not doing so earlier.

I just wish that we got to see the two his childhood friend Kai continue their journey together without the guilt setting in on Kei.

Title: Noragami 01 (Noragami: Stray God, #1)
Author: Adachitoka
My Review:
Noragami means "Stray God" and its quite fitting.

The set up is everything. I watched the anime years ago yet failed to ever pick this manga up despite that cliffhanger..

Needless to say, I love the panels and stunning art work. I love the characters and their complexities. They make the world of Noragami so much more. The insight each character add gives to building the world and its problems and I love the slow burn of it.

Yato the stray god has fallen out of favor as times have changed; however, he hasn't given up and faded from existence. He lives on through the small favors and wishes requested of him. It's honest work and it's touching how he yearns for recognition (even if it is just one single person).

I love the plot twist Hiyori adds to the already full plate Yato has. She becomes half-dead too easily (her body falls asleep and her spirit roams free) and it poses a risk of her accidentally putting herself in danger. Not only is her tail the only thing keeping her tethered to the world of the living but also attracts too much attention from the other spirits (the corrupted ones). Yukine is adorable as a little spirit but very angsty as a teen. He's still very adorable. I cant wait to see how this develops and grows each of them through their adventures together.

Title: Ajin: Demi-Human, Vol. 2 (Ajin: Demi-Human, #2)
Author: Gamon Sakurai
My Review:
I think I liked this volume a lot more than the first. It dove straight into what exactly everyone's motives were and how this society views Demi-Humans.

First, let's discuss Kei. Let's keep in mind he's 17 and just a high schooler with dreams of becoming a doctor. He gets into an accident and "becomes a monster". We have reasons to believe he's almost always had this inside him and after dying and returning, he knows now what he is. He hasn't left humanity which is probably the most significant "obstacle" for the majority of the other characters. He cares for his little sister (who is later revealed to have an extremely rare disease that he wants to cure her of by becoming a doctor). He cares for his childhood friend who he even left behind thinking he would be endangering him. There's so much depth to him that hasn't been broken and that's where the heartbreak begins.

He's betrayed by his fellow demi-humans and is let experimented on... It's unnerving to read about and see happening. I can't imagine his anguish and pain. Yet he doesn't kill anyone. He doesn't do it even when he was that close, because he's afraid to disappoint those he loves and cares for. He would become a monster only then. It's heartbreaking to see and I had wondered if there was any one who even cared for him the way he did. He genuinely saw and treated others as his own fellow humans because he saw himself as one as well. He wasn't acting differently to hide something he didn't know he was.

I liked the tiny segment of his former classmate signing a petition and sympathizing with the demi-humans (though I guess it was a bit fruitless and it was really just for Kei only).

I do really like seeing Nakamura's current state and past. He doesn't flinch at death and uses it to his advantage... It's scary. It's clear that he's disconnected from humanity and it's what makes him such a powerful opponent. That fight scene was something of awe and its just as terrifying to think that's who you'd be messing with.

"Be more human than the humans." Yet his every action is getting further and further from that ideal moto of his...

Nakamura's back story was tragic. I just could not believe that twist. His helmet.HAD HIS HEAD IN IT. MY JAW DROPPED. He didn't notice...he genuinely thought he just lost his arm.. I just stopped and stared speechless. The loss he experienced in that moment would have been tremendous and the fastest way to break his soul. It puts into perspective how he is wired and how he came to develop his mindset. I'm officially hooked now after this volume.

I can't wait to read the next one.

Title: Ajin: Demi-Human, Vol. 4 (Ajin: Demi-Human, #4)
Author: Gamon Sakurai
My Review:
I instantly liked that duo of the firefighter and that teen. I have a serious growing hate for Sato (Nakamura). I don't like how things are progressing and this is just the first chapter. The firefighter isn't wrong with it becoming a witch hunt further with a public terrorist attack on innocent people.

I'm dead that the teen, Nakano, is essentially saved by his caring neighbor who calls in for an ambulance at the right moment. He dies and notices the oozing of matter that fixes him. It immediately reminds him of what he saw in the train in the distance. It's nice details that I crave. Immediately after the doctors just let him go.. It's the most unrealistic thing I've see in this Manga yet.

AHH The part Tanaka tells the girls not to go see the cops guarding the building.. He's subconscious self knew he doesn't want innocents to die.. The plane hijacking... This is going to be an all-out war and disaster on so many levels for everyone...

"The thrill of it."

That's the voice of someone who's too far gone and beyond saving at this point.

Title: Ajin: Demi-Human, Vol. 5 (Ajin: Demi-Human, #5)
Author: Gamon Sakurai
My Review:
There's a lot of character-building in this volume. Sato declares war on the humans and we get to see how the SAT handles him. If tranquilizer guns are illegal they needed to keep killing Sato fast enough to not let him react. That doesn't, however, take into account other demi-humans being involved.

On the other hand, we get to see how Kai handles the news (which is pretty cold in my opinion). The kid that was saved by the firefighter is trapped in the truck which is mundane but we realize the biggest plot hole would have been him using an IBM (or Black Ghost). We later find out that he can't conjure one for some reason but he can see them.

The demi-humans (Sato) write up a hit list and soon after the targets realize that it's not in order. That any one of them can be next and it put Tosaki into a panic. Kai reaches out to Tosaki and proposes the idea of an immortal army in exchange for victory on their terms. The deal only goes through because of Nakano. He's earning a spot on the "best boy" title.

It's a good volume and it leaves me wanting to see more action again. It was a lot of violence at the start and then it simmers down with some hiding and finally a car ride with many questions hanging in the air.

Title: Ajin: Demi-Human, Vol. 6 (Ajin: Demi-Human, #6)
Author: Gamon Sakurai
My Review:
"Let your heart guide you and you face ruin"; I've finally read this infamous line. It's a classic spin on "emotions are weaknesses and they lead you down an unreliable path".

Kaito is back and.. he's in prison... for helping a demi-human escape. But there we meet someone really interesting...

It seems Kai is making allies and Kei has no clue how much his friend cares for his sorry butt.

Title: 亜人 7 (Ajin: Demi-Human, #7)
Author: Gamon Sakurai
My Review:
How does Kai survive all the time and what is this safe place he always talks about getting to...? Is it really important for Nagai Kei to go there or not?

Regardless this volume was just giving me more assurance that Sato is crazy from the start and he's a terrifying monster to go up against. I seriously feel for that Vietnam soldier who went on that rescue mission that could have gone perfectly if Sato hadn't snapped... Or maybe that was the intent, make it seem like it was going perfectly to give everyone a sense of peace before risking it all for that rush and forcing everyone around him to accept his help still in the situation he caused.

In the end, I just really hate everyone involved with Sato. Including that IT guy who could have lived a nice life working at The Forge, but decided to just end it all by going awol... It ticks me off a lot being so intelligent but choosing stupidity.

That Tanaka guy needs a serious backbone and figure out what he wants other than trying to figure Sato's plans out. It won't end well for him at this point.

Title: My Clueless First Friend 01
Author: Taku Kawamura
My Review:
Volume 1 Chapters 1-18 Completed!
Gosh, Taiyo Takada is literally warm sunshine on a cold winter day. He is the absolute sweetest. Nishimura is also so cute and all the little kids are brats for being so mean despite not knowing her. They tease her, make fun of her relentlessly, and isolate her in class. Everyone needs a Taiyo or needs to be a Taiyo.
He's living his best life not caring a bit about others' prejudice and becoming friends with those who are kind to him. His using the bully's words against them is also so satisfying. It gives him leverage against them by using their words against them. Nishimura and Takada will be great friends so a long time (Hopefully, no unintentionally friend-zoning each other but in a safe healthy loving relationship in whatever form that might be).

Title: Tokyo Ghoul, Tome 1 (Tokyo Ghoul, #1)
Author: Sui Ishida
My Review: Gosh I’m so happy to have picked this up! I needed to know what I would be getting myself into when watching/reading Tokyo Ghoul and this has been a perfect introduction. The perfect set up for a half human and half ghoul. The struggles of hiding in plain sight and also learning to control his insatiable appetite. The struggles of becoming something different than before and learning to accept it at the cost of losing his previous life.

The two investigators are creepy asf. The senior guy looks like he's lost a few screws since the 1800s and the other guy looks like an arrogant try-hard. They both piss me off every time they're on screen.

I'll continue reading~

Title: Leveling Up My Husband to the Max Vol. 1 (novel) (English Edition)
Author: Nuova
My Review:
-ill come back to this as soon as i can to edit but brief points to touch on:
So season one was super satisfying.
Female lead is introduced with a certain goal and attitude to accomplish that specific goal.
The male lead is highly misunderstood. however the two leads actually communicate and talk out all their conflicts and internal issues with the other.
The villain that's introduced is cleanly dealt with by the end of the volume and its satisfying to see it followed out without extreme consequences.
Its revealed however there is a bigger scheme behind the scenes and the leads will need each other to make it out in one piece unscathed.

==
Whole Series Completed!!

The communication between both the female and male lead will be my favorite of all manhwas. They are not extraordinary but simple people with a simple goal in mind. It’s almost humble they want a life together without fear and threat of war and famine for their sub-country. I enjoyed all the moments between the two and more so as the story evolved. The villains were great and all.. but it felt so pitiful..

It’s almost like secondhand embarrassment when it comes to the Emperor and his reason for hating Carlyx and his nation. It was out of jealousy and it's embarrassing… Saw his love as an object and threw a temper tantrum when she rejected his advances. When she did give in to his fear, he betrayed his word first. He went after Carlyx’s grandfather out of spite and it's disgusting that he couldn’t take a damn no.

That’s next-level arrogance and pathetic to be taking out your anger cause you couldn’t have what you want… He deserved a worse death. Fucking mocked death to the end cause he genuinely thinks he’s in the right for hurting innocent people just cause he can. It’s beyond me how he even contributed to making the 5th prince.

And it’s also beyond me how the 5th prince’s mother even loved the emperor to his last breath. Red Flag was there… just ignored in vain.

A ton of that was ranting that you'll probably agree to after finishing the series. Overall fantastic read! Highly Recommended!

Title: 하루만 네가 되고 싶어 2 [Haruman Naega Doego Sip-eo 2] (Your Throne, #2)
Author: SAM
My Review:
Chapter 13-23 Complete!

The two female leads, Medea and Psyche, are breaking my heart. Their backgrounds, their twists of fate, and the consequences of manipulation are heartbreaking. All men in this WEBTOON deserve a purge (minus precious Helios).

The wit in this is incredible and beautifully crafted into a masterpiece. The way each side’s decisions and actions are laid out and slowly changing each other’s perception is beautiful, to say the least.

I don’t like this god in this WEBTOON. Obviously, they already play favorites but it’s rubbing me the wrong way. The deity might not have been punishing Medea but you can sense the underlying tension between them. The god used Medea to save Psyche and saw the opportunity when Medea wished to switch lives. Over all the deity only cared about Psyche and was biased since the beginning. Always painting Psyche's story as the more pitiful one yet right now Medea is more pitiful being used once again to save someone else's life.

I’ll be continuing to root for Medea and Psyche’s improvement and goals. I want the prince Dead.

It’s not a request. Prince should die with no mercy. He is picture book psychotic and cruel/calculating. There is no doubt that he and Medea’s dad are villains. You can’t deny that this a**hat of a prince is clever and brilliant. It makes the stakes that much more terrifying.

Title: 하루만 네가 되고 싶어 3 [Haruman Naega Doego Sip-eo 3] (Your Throne, #3)
Author: SAM
My Review:
Chapters 24-35

Learning the difference between love and manipulation is the first step to understanding the abuse you've been through and the start to actually healing. My love for both Medea and psyche are only growing by the days...

In another note, Helios is shaping up to be the only man up to standards every other man seems damn problematic... The new red head introduced in this volume seems... Interesting. I'm not making any calls yet but I'm weary from the track record all these men hold (exception being only Helios).

We are introduced to a larger scheme taking place involving the problematic imperial family and the church and the divine powers.

Psyche and Medea are both fighting their predicaments and it's refreshing to see.. Especially for Psyche..

Medea and Helios have a true love.
No one can convince me otherwise. I strive to love someone and be loved like they show through their words and actions..
Being able to love someone's soul and body differently is such a beautiful thing...to love someone's soul means to love that person no matter how they look and it's just really stuck to me..

One day..

Title: 消えた初恋 5 [Kieta Hatsukoi 5]
Author: Wataru Hinekure

There’s 2 arcs in this that I really loved. The tutor arc and the restaurant arc.

I reread the tutor arc so often like no joke. The phobia was handled so well and I love their little friend group very much. They support and care for each other despite other people’s preconceived beliefs and opinions. I’m glad it was cleared up and Okano’s character could be redeemed 🥰. And the bonus relationship progression 😭🥰!!

The jealousy Ida had 😍🥰 I squealed. Literally fangirling cause man could not handle the whispering between Aoki with his competition 😆😂. Title: 消えた初恋 4 [Kieta Hatsukoi 4]
Author: Wataru Hinekure
Additional Authors: Aruko, ひねくれ渡, アルコ
My Review:
Christmas arc! I like how they resolved the issue with going about telling others about their relationship status not as a way to feel ashamed or insecure about their sexual orientation but rather as a form of communication and consideration for the other. I only had a gripe with how Ida never really said he liked Aoki back when officially dating. They are taking it really slow and the way it was broken down and discussed was poetic in a way. I really adored how this whole volume was written and explained through conversations.

I’m lowkey kinda worried for the next arc now though just as I thought we were getting somewhere with our main couple.

Title: 消えた初恋 3 [Kieta Hatsukoi 3]
Author: Wataru Hinekure
Additional Authors: Aruko, ひねくれ渡, アルコ
My Review:
This one was ok.

We get to see more progress for our main couple and secondary couple 🤩!

The misunderstandings are surprisingly cleared up almost immediately or actively worked on by both parties and it’s heartwarming. The drama of if they do or don’t doesn’t linger forever like other webtoons/manga.

Very enjoyable but nothing spectacular/stunning like the other two volumes. Feels like we’re starting to settle in and see how this goes now on and it’s good progress for their respective relationships.

Title: 消えた初恋 2 [Kieta Hatsukoi 2]
Author: Wataru Hinekure
Additional Authors: Aruko, ひねくれ渡, アルコ
My Review:
I love how everyone is actually making an effort to talk it through and understand how the people they care about feel. This volume had me choked up for a minute with how the misunderstanding was being misunderstood even if it was coming from someone who didn’t mean to hurt Aoki.

Though I may have not liked how Hashimoto smacked Aida, she reasonably got through to him when explaining how being afraid to talk about one’s feelings may not be easy especially infront of others you respect and care for.. it’s not an excuse to run away or preserve themselves from pain bc we can see Aoki internally burning up by hiding away the truth. He was an afraid of letting everyone down and by the end we see Aida and Aoki patching up the situation (Best moment of the volume in my opinion).

Aida is dense asf but he really came through for his buddy when it counts. I’m glad how this was handled 😌 it shaping up to be one of favorite reads of the genre (BL) as a whole honestly.

The ending of the volume has me a bit joyful despite how rough the relationship is going so far between Ida and Aoki. He’s starting to see the nuances of catching feelings and I’m here for the show 🍿👀

Title: 消えた初恋 9 [Kieta Hatsukoi 9]
Author: Wataru Hinekure
Additional Authors: Aruko, ひねくれ渡, アルコ
My Review:
The 9 year time skip had me SCARED 😨 literally heart wrenching to see how much Aoki had suddenly changed from spring 2nd year to winter 3rd year during the amnesia. In the event that they had broken up I honestly don’t know how Ida would react other than mourning his first love the entire time and taking anything Aoki gives him gratefully. I’m glad that was all a hallucination on Ida’s end.

Ida has gotten better with expressing himself and easier to read his feelings/emotions. I can’t believe how Ida used to say that he didn’t know how one feels affection for another person to how absolutely whipped he is for Aoki now in current day. Aoki is adorable but definitely has grown more confident in himself and his relationships, maturity makes him so attractive. I’m glad he has gotten more confident in himself and their relationship to tell his family. I had wished he could be more honest with his worries and troubles this entire time and he’s finally gotten there now in the final volume.

I’m glad this ended on a much much happier note with the time capsule scene and things looking bright for both the couples. I’m happy and overall quite pleased with how the author decided on handling the storyline and their intimate moments. I literally wish them the absolute best in their live on the pages of their world. I would read a spin off or a continuation of this series any day! 🥰

I don’t mind reading something similar to this again ❤️

Title: 消えた初恋 8 [Kieta Hatsukoi 8]

Additional Authors: Aruko, ひねくれ渡, アルコ

Title: 아빠, 나 이 결혼 안할래요! 4 [Appa, Na I Gyeolhon An Hallaeyo! 4]
Author: Yuri .
My Review:
Volume 4
Chapters 48-64

We get a lot of lore drop in this one, but it's all very enjoyable regardless. The jokes and misunderstandings are just tragically hilarious. Legis has been best dad from the start and we're staring to see Juvellian see it for herself slowly but surely. Max is straight up the most delusionally optimistic ML I've read. I needed a break from the choppy translations, but this is a work of art now that I'm rereading it after so many years.

Title: Father, I don't want this marriage T07
Author: Yuri .
My Review:
Volume 7
Chapter 97-112

AWW Juvellian and her father are officially on fantastic terms after the big reveal in Juvel's past memories. I love how much depth was put into why Juvel thought she had been reincarnated into a book and how time started over for her and the big reveal Legis' first life after Juvel's death . I couldn't stop my tears in this volume. I kid you not, the scenes with the Floyens and their tragic past are heartwrenching to the point it's taking my heart out of commission.

What makes it one of my favorite novels so far is the way everyone makes sense and how nuanced the emotions of each character feel to me. I feel anguish for Legis and Amelia. I catch myself smiling whenever Max is goofy with his "father-in-law" when proclaiming his unabashed love for Juvel. If glares could kill, Max would have died and revived constantly on every page.

The lore on Floyens is just getting started, and it's crazy how the story is unfolding thus far. I'm unable to keep my awe at how well crafted this story is and the love put in by both author and artist. I hope the plan to save Legis is going to happen without a hitch... But there's still so much story left.. I'm rooting for the wolf, the cats, and the lovely mouse!

Title: 아빠, 나 이 결혼 안할래요! 8 [Appa, Na I Gyeolhon An Hallaeyo! 8]
Author: Yuri .
My Review:
Volume 8
113-123 and all the side stories, I read all 8

Go ahead and rip my heart out. I laughed and cried constantly. The ending for the emperor was too short, but I'm glad it was Legis who did him in. Mikhail's ending was satisfactory. I was truly pleased with how Fafnil was handled and how the Goddess and Juvelle's mother played a part. The last main line chapter, which is about Juvelle and Max's wedding, felt so deserving.

The ending side stories .... They made me tear up and laugh all the same. Max really is out here manifesting his future though because he said he would love to have a boy and a girl (preferably twins)!! I just have a goofy smile seeing how things played out for everyone. It's a bittersweet parting from one of the best reads of my summer 2025. Ik I'll come back and re-read for Max, Juvelle, and her father too <3 <3.

Just a silly love story with a thousand misunderstandings about a cat, a mouse, a wolf, and a squirrel. Read it if you want a fully completed translated manhwa to binge.

Title: 이번 생은 가주가 되겠습니다 1 [Ibeon Saeng-eun Gajuga Doegessseubnida 1] (I Shall Master this Family, Vol. 1)
Author: Ro-a Kim
My Review:
Season One chapters 1-51 are complete!

I love love love the art style to death! It's clean and very cute.

FL is exceptionally intelligent, however, it seems from her first life she fell victim to a lot of abuse and was very much complacent to all the events that surrounded her family's/her downfall. In the second life, she is given a chance to start anew from 10 years old by making changes to the dreary future. She has a lot she needs to accomplish starting with saving her father's life from an illness, making a place for herself in the list of potential heirs to Lombardy, and lastly avoiding Lombardy's downfall by supporting the right side of the Royal heirs (Supporting Perez over the other prick of a prince).

She's so cute and I'd do anything for all the cutesy father-daughter moments (again I pray her father doesn't die like the first life). I love her manipulativeness; it's great to see her getting revenge one by one without anyone suspecting much at all. She's slowly winning over the Lombardy Title and it makes me so proud!!

I thoroughly enjoyed this first season and look forward to Season 2's release!

Title: トモちゃんは女の子! 1 [Tomo-chan wa Onna no ko 1] (Tomo-chan is a girl!, #1)
Author: Fumita Yanagida
My Review:
Chapter 001-125 + Omake!

This was such a great first volume with a great way to introduce all the characters and all of the overarching problems, but in particular that Jun doesn't see Tomo-chan as a girl. It's so cute and comedic! I love Tomo-chan's whole personality and behavior. She also looks so so cool. Jun is hilariously in denial. The Omake of the volume definitely catches on to that also. Gundo is best girl. I personally think she her bad personality is her selling point. I love her for her cold relentless and downright sinister mind... Carol, I had mixed feeling about at first but she's definitely growing on me. She has her moments to shine and she is way smarter than I originally thought.

Needless to say, read this! There's a manga adaption being uploaded at the moment and it's that slice-of-life comedy we need at times like this.

Title: Skip and Loafer, Vol. 1
Author: Misaki Takamatsu
My Review:
I picked this manga up after seeing the anime on Crunchyroll. It's so refreshing to see not only all characters fleshed out but each with personal goals and problems they tackle head-on. The interactions feel so natural and light. It gives me nostalgia about those high school days with every panel. The art style is just as it is on the cover and dare I say it gets better and better every page. (The same can be said about the anime!)
I find myself smiling and happy with Mitsumi's small accomplishments and friendships. Its so endearing to see them all bond so closely and root for all of them.

The first 12 episodes of the anime cover up to Volume 4's finale. That said I will make it short: WATCH THE SHOW. READ THE MANGA.

It's not a threat... really. It's characters that can actually talk it out. They can actually act on their words and have a goal they all reach towards. It's not solely focused on having a boyfriend or relationship. It's not making pointless friendships that are shallow. It's not riddled with lackluster plot points that won't break or build the characters. They feel so real and lovely. I can't help but keep wanting this to never end.

Title: 하루만 네가 되고 싶어 1 [Haruman Naega Doego Sip-eo 1] (Your Throne, #1)
Author: SAM
My Review:
Chapter 1-12 Complete!
The way this WEBTOON hurt me. I didn’t know how much I loved complicated characters that aren’t completely good and completely evil until this WEBTOON.

The twist of fate and the cruel nature of the way they were brought up is insanely moving. The backgrounds of both Medea and Psyche shed light on their stakes and positions. The potential both of them have makes me want to root for both of them.

There’s just no way to explain how incredible the writing of both those characters were. They became memorable the moment I realized how much potential each gal had bring out their knives. I need to really digest this but read this.

It’s been 12 chapters. I’m hooked and I’m not ready for this to end.

Title: Death's Game T01 (1)
Author: Wonsik Lee
My Review:
TRIGGER WARNINGS!! Not for those that can't handle death whether suicide, murder, or accidental.

Brilliant writing. It’s flawless from start to end. It contains trauma wrapped in every life the main character Yijae Choi encounters. Mind you, the reason why he is even trapped and forced to endure each of these lives is his punishment for choosing suicide. He needs to understand from start to end that his decisions reflect on more than just him. Each life is carefully chosen and perfectly executed. Executed might not be the best phrase here, but whatever. It had me gripping my seat from start to end.

The goal of the author and artist was absolutely covered and they hit it on the mark.
There is only ONE of you. Only ONE life.

Title: 네가 죽기를 바랄때가 있었다 1 [Nega Juggireul Baralddaega Isseossda 1] (Wished You Were Dead [Novel], #1)
Author: Jin Seo
My Review:
Currently reading the webtoon translation:

I'll count this as volume 1:
"The King Hates the Queen" 1-10

The initial step up has me questioning whether this king really is intelligent. He isn't quick on the uptake at all. At first, it was essentially a version of Remarried Empress but now it's just disappointing me... The clear signs of abuse the Queen is experiencing and the King is just blinded by his rage and anger towards her father is just incomprehensible. Like hate on her father, that's fair we all don't like him and he's do nothing to us. However, the King is taking out his anger on Evonne and it's heartbreaking. She's being used by both sides (and I'm starting to think the same for the concubine being in on it as well).

I'll give my predictions:
The King's buddy from the past is 100% Evonne who was just dressed as a boy back then. She saved or helped him, but he can't remember anything about her.

The concubine is under a contract with the King, but that one scene where she says she's become the King's pawn in a moment of desperation is giving me the vibes that she's playing 4d chess. She might love the King but is playing it off at least to retain some power for her family's name. She might have made her own letter depicting the poisoning and made sure the Queen had the poisoned glass.

Evonne knowing full well her glass was poisoned... and still drinking it... girlie wanted to die off from this life. I really feel for her and her suffering. She can't leave the palace not out of greed, but her father ain't gonna take her back. Who in their right mind would shelter a deposed queen? She has no where to go... Telling Evonne to disappear is the equivalent of telling her to die if she wants out.

King acting love sick? Give me a break, he has no right to feel for Evonne after what he put her through. Now him, using her feelings and disadvantage to his benefit, disgusts me. He's playing her and he even acknowledged that it would be cruel of him to take everything from her and he STILL does it..

This is gonna be a long read. Hopefully, it gets better for Evonne, the misunderstandings are pissing me off.

Title: 아빠, 나 이 결혼 안할래요! 1 [Appa, Na I Gyeolhon An Hallaeyo! 1]
Author: Yuri .
My Review:
Volume 1
Chapters 1-14

We start with Jubelian’s tragic end, a brutal culmination of misunderstandings and neglect. After being sent back in time, we’re quickly shown the central problem: her and her father’s complete inability to communicate.

Mikhail, the original male lead, is introduced and is so clearly unhinged it’s baffling he was ever seen as romantic interest material.

Then enters Max—who tries to assassinate her in her sleep—and whom Jubelian hilariously mistakes for her dad’s favorite student. Naturally, he starts falling for her soon after.

A dramatic, chaotic, and ironically romantic start. Definitely a fun ride ahead.

Title: 악녀를 죽여 줘 2 [Agnyeoreul Jugyeo Jwo 2]
Author: Haegi
My Review:
Eris is so consistent in her convictions to leave this world makes me so proud of her. She is unlike most other female leads. She doesn't sit around and adapt to her shitty role. She actively works against it with her life on the line.

Like seriously, she hates everyone in this world so it makes sense for her to leave as desperately as she is trying to. Her goal is to gain an understanding of the other characters and use them to achieve her motives: leave this world. It's a breath of fresh air. Who would have known craving the death of the main character you're reading about would be so satisfying and heartbreaking? I want Eris to escape not because I grew to hate her but because of the complete opposite. I wish to see her happy genuinely without fear or pain. If that means she needs to die, then please do.

Ankin is too good for these people. He deserves his own happily ever after with Eris after she escapes the story. It doesn't look like the story is heading in that direction, but I digress. Ankin is ever loyal and charming. His constant care for his master warms my heart and also breaks it. You can tell the "lovely feelings" are all there without saying the words. I want closure but I fear how that would play out. Confessing wouldn't exactly hinder Eris' plans, but they aren't going to continue blossoming. It's a situation like nipping a bud before it's ready to bloom; the pain of separating will be greater than my heart can bear.

The prince. It's undeniable how worthless he's become with every appearance. Just calling him 'trash' would be too high of a compliment for him. I loathe every interaction he has with anyone. It's a pity Helena is paired with him. I do hope his worthless face gets wiped off the map. I would love to continue bashing that 'thing', but it would take years. I will settle by simply saying he is worth none of my time and energy. When he is dead, no tears should be shed. It's not worth it.

On to season 3! Looking forward to Eris' plan of ultimate revenge and also hopefully (&sadly) bringing an end to 'Lady Eris' in this world.

Title: My Clueless First Friend 04

Volume 4 Chapter 41-50 Complete!

This volume is about the school sports festival and all the races and class competitions wrapped into one. We already know Takada is a very fast runner and it’s already determined that he would be participating in the baton race.

Then there’s a sudden twist! He breaks his arm trying to save Nishimura! She’s overrun with guilt but also makes a realization that she wants to be discovering and living out her youth with him. Not just have him do things for her.

I love the bully redemption arc that takes place within this volume as well and it’s interesting and adorable in its own right.

Kasahara isn’t so bad after all.

Title: 외과의사 엘리제 4 (Doctor Elise: The Royal Lady with the Lamp, Vol. 4)
Author: Yuin
My Review:
Hands down one of the best-completed manhwa's out there.
Having lived life like a spoiled brat and died a miserable death, Elise reincarnates into the modern world where she is alone with no family to call her own. She works harder than most and climbs her way to the top in the medical profession. One day on an airplane, she is suddenly met with turbulence and dies and finds herself back into her original life as Elise. Not wanting the same fate as her first life, she quickly starts making changes to her life for the better. She not only gets the main lead this time but saves countless lives on the battlefields and through medical science. "Mother of Modern Medicine" "Lady with the lamp"<- refers to her time spent caring for wounded soldiers during the war. She's honestly so inspiring!
The main character Elise is a hard worker and deserves the best in the world. The main leads complement each other so well and all of the supporting characters are so loveable as well. There were moments of bliss and heartache throughout the entire 143 chapters. I seriously can't believe it took me so long to sit down and write a review on this work of art.

Title: 彼女が公爵邸に行った理由 4 (フロース コミック) [Kanojo ga Kōshaku-Tei ni Itta Riyū 4]
Author: Whale
My Review:
Alright, Final Season 4 (chapters 122-148) plus side stories completed!!

What a journey... This was one of the better reads of the year by far. It took a while to get through but the attention to detail on this was amazing. I love the lovey scenes this season haha. It, in the end, was very satisfying and I'm a sucker for soulmates forever even in a different life story. I enjoyed it and do recommend this since again it's completed entirely. It's well worth your time and energy.

Main Female Lead Raeliana isn't a pushover and never has been. She takes charge and puts her words into action (she can shoot a gun with no problem) she won't sit back and let someone step all over her. Main Male Lead Noah has never been a tragic character (no childhood issues and even has a sweet older brother) but his heart-warming up to Raeliana over time just makes me so happy. It's a book filled with strong characters all with them serving their parts well and overall happy with the structure of the story as well.

Title: 彼女が公爵邸に行った理由 3 (フロース コミック) [Kanojo ga Kōshaku-Tei ni Itta Riyū 3]
Author: Whale
My Review:
Season 3 chapters 81-121 completed!

This was such an eye-opening season... The truth of the world is starting to unravel and I'm not sure how I'm gonna be able to take it. Noah is starting to open up to a new side of Raeliana and the same goes for her as well. I'm also so so glad that the mystery behind Beatrice is starting to build up tension in the manga now also.

Things are changing in this world and fast. Events that were not meant to happen yet are arriving faster and Beatrice is making her move into the main story now at this point. I'm not sure why things are happening the way they are but I can not wait till this all boils over.. for better or worse I'm looking forward to the new season as well as dreading how it will unfold.

Title: 古見さんは、コミュ症です。 volume 13
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
Rei is a sweetheart! Rei is having trouble adjusting to all the different environments and people because of her parents moving around so often for work. Rei lashes out in anger that she shouldn't be friends with anyone since they will all forget her anyway or she will have to move on regardless of the bonding. Eventually, Komi and Rei do sync and begin communicating very well. It was like a sisterly bond and it was really endearing!

I do hope Rei will have a lot of fun making as many friends as Osana all over the globe and come back to visit Komi again soon. There were really sweet moments together like playing together and sleeping to comfort the other. The only thing I gotta say is that the mock pokemon were creepy funny as hell and that Shosuke is boss at being good a random sh**. Like who the hell is good at engraving rice... He's another level and I understand Rei's fascination with him. I truly am amused by him too.

Title: Why Raeliana Ended Up at the Duke's Mansion, Vol. 2
Author: Whale
My Review:
Chapters 51-87 are complete!

Raeliana's soul is rejecting her new body and it seems that it has something to do with the bigger plot of the story (A dark sorceress being manipulated by a candidate of the King). The original FL might actually be connected to Raeliana also since in the short moment she appeared (it's mentioned that she fainted right after we know Raeli also fainted for 10 days).

I love-hate the awkward moments both Raeli and the Duke share. Taylor isn't in the story often enough to make up for the sadness of the situation, but his Holiness is back this season! He is truly a sweet soul and I love how understanding/comforting he is for Raeli.

I do have to say Sir Wheaton really stepped it up this season. His reactions and involvement in the shadows I gotta love it. He's just too funny and sweet. I thoroughly enjoyed him more this time around.

Jason head of the royal guard is overstepping so many of his boundaries. He knows very well Raeli's complicated situation but he insists on only courting someone who's taken. Duke is really really harsh towards his supposed competition. "It looks like it isn't Raeliana's. What I mean is, what you have around your neck, cannot possibly belong to Raeliana." Duke becoming more and more possessive each season.

Title: The Abandoned Empress, Vol. 2
Author: Ina
My Review:
Season Two Chapters 47-87 completed! I really don't like how Allendis is getting so obsessed with Aristia! He honestly is so two-faced and fake with Aristia that it's frustrating me. I'd like it a lot more if he was as he is with everyone else towards her. It would be a hell lot more respectful of all the trust she puts in him. I like her dynamic with Carsein a heck lot more. He is very straightforward and is the same with everyone. He works hard towards his ambitions while keeping true to his personality and self when he's around Aristia. I'm looking forward to the next season (3rd) with Carsein is on the cover with her. Even if Carsein isn't her match romantically he beside her as a loyal friend and companion are enough for me. Allendis needs to take a few steps back on the other hand. He's just giving me weird possessive and controlling vibes since the first season with his and Carsein's face off.

The prince is interesting. He's just as dull as you'd expect with little to go on him. He's just changing and noticing Aristia more now in this life because she's acting differently. She is different hence he's changed too. It would have been better to see Aristia controlling the situation with the same attitude as in the past life. Not really attitude but personality. Her Ice Queen nature shouldn't have disappeared completely resulting in a completely new Aristia. If we saw the prince falling for the original Ice Queen and her rejecting him still would have been a far more satisfying result of her second life.

Title: 古見さんは、コミュ症です。 volume 12
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
This volume wasn't spent proactively making new friends, just spending some time with her current friend group. The little game they played all the way to the beach was fun to see. I ship Naruse and Ase.. they seem very cute together..

TadanoXKom is a slow struggle. Manbagi is cute but she isn't the perfect match for Tadano. It's gonna hurt like ripping off wax... Cause Komi and her are very close and having those feeling grow will only hurt them both and heart isn't ready. Seems like the same goes for the author since we have a new little arc coming up.

Rei is new character introduced towards the end of the volume!

Title: 古見さんは、コミュ症です。 volume 11
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
This volume is a favorite.

Cold and in an isolated cabin with rain outside and a single blanket to share? Yet Komi and Tadano are progressing like ants.. Not that that is bad or anything, just don't your hopes up. The younger Komi-Tadano couple also get the limelight for a little moment. Hence I'm satisfied with the volume~.

Title: 古見さんは、コミュ症です。 volume 10
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
New year, New class, New People.

Big changes happened this Volume! We are met with a new class full of new people and some old which will be a challenge to both Komi and Tadano. One Komi's journey to 100 friends we will surely meet with a lot more diverse characters and first up is Manbagi!

Komi's first friend without Tadano's assistance. This was such a pivotal moment. I am so proud of Komi! Manbagi is so so much better off without all that makeup, why did no one stop this poor child!? I do sense some love-triangle brewing so I'm not sure where this will go other than heartbreak... but this is the first friendship without Tadano's help (;_;)...

Title: 古見さんは、コミュ症です。 volume 9
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
Valentine's is the most anticipated event of high school. The poor guys waiting for their own chocolates (but probably wouldn't get any) and then the girls happily handing them out like goddesses. Yamai.. she's getting creepier and creepier each time I see her on scene. I wish I could forget her, but she's made it to the cover this volume (the one on the floor trying to get an upskirt shot of Komi).

Tadano and Komi moments are cute. but I have to say some of these Katai and Tadano bro moments got me haha.

I'd enjoy it a lot more without a certain person..

Title: Komi Can't Communicate, Vol. 8
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
The standard Kyoto Class Trip! It's not too memorable but the scene with the guys all being guys... It got me cracking up for a minute.

We have a new character Naruse the Narcissist for this volume! We also get a cute Kometani the Commenter. Naruse talks but doesn't listen (yet another communication issue here..) Kometani is just struggling from the sidelines as we watch Naruse fail to woo Komi (LOL main character of his own little world). It's good to see Tadano's own friend group slowly increase with the addition of new characters too.

Title: Komi Can't Communicate, Vol. 7
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
The snowfall fight was everything.. Silent Killer Komi is just utter perfection. Yamai's fatal flaw to take out her own teammates to indulge Komi backfires and it's a moment to cherish.

Christmas party at Komi's place clashes with Komi's BDay! Komi goes out on a shopping spree with her brother and just like with her father's shopping day this was a sweet moment as well. I love Komi's reaction to the bday gift. its the highlight of the volume for me.

Tadano and Komi's relationship haven't progressed much, but the slow build-up is definitely well worth it for the smaller moments they share.

Title: Komi Can't Communicate, Vol. 6
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
The maid cafe is done and to celebrate (though due to a certain someone causing trouble with ticket sales Komi's class doesn't win) everyone goes to Karaoke, perfect for Komi who can barely converse a few sentences.

The 3 delinquents' delusions of lovely interactions with the girls of the class are interesting. Some are honestly very cute and I would happily ship where others are a bit too delusional.

Katai is a new character! He struggles like Komi, but unlike the elegant queen herself Katai comes off as a straight-up gangster... He looks terrifying and his inability to communicate just put that over the top. Luckily, we have our room reader Tadano to be his best friend and ease him into class and school. Katai is delusioned to think that Komi-san is his Master giving him the staredown, but she is equally as terrified as anyone else (minus Tadano cause he's Tadano). He's fun and and new dynamic character for the school setting I can't wait to see more of him.

My favorite moments had to be the Cat Cafe with Chocolate and the hot potatoes scene..

Title: 古見さんは、コミュ症です。volume 5 (Komi-san wa Komyushou Desu., #5)
Author: Tomohito Oda
My Review:
Komi experiences jealousy! I like that Komi is at least aware of her growing fondness and romantic feelings towards Tadano. There are a lot of dense characters out there and Komi isn't one, thankfully. She notices Onemine getting closer to Tadano and as a twist { Onemine figures out pretty quickly that Komi like likes Tadano more than a friend and Onemine like a big sister supports the ship! Gotta love girls supporting other girls! }

Title: Coraline
Author: Neil Gaiman
My Review: The novel started off slow to emphasize Coraline’s, not Coroline, life in an attempt to juxtapose her extremely to a life she actually wants. It’s interesting to see how though she likes the other world, she prefers her real parents and refuses the affection of the other mother adamantly. Her personality is not one that I relate to well, but she does have her moments to shine. I especially loved her telling of the story of her father and the wasps and how she described what it means to be brave.“When you’re scared but you still do it anyway, that’s brave.” It’s for that reason that she faces what she must in order to bring her life back to normal. A good little book ensnared in a web of wonder and fantasy. I’m intrigued by the mystery and magic that surrounds the corridor between the two worlds and the little pocket dimension inside the well. A fantastic book for a little night scare. I remember when I was little that I was absolutely entranced by the movie and how I begged my parents to let me watch it over and over. After growing up, I’ve learned to appreciate the beauty of the whole affair even more than before. The movie and the book in their own merit hold up to be so much more than the eye can see.

Watching him evolve from a one-note comic relief guy into someone who’s genuinely trying to step up for his friends has been so satisfying. Title: ブスに花束を。(5) (角川コミックス・エース) (Japanese Edition)
Author: 作楽ロク
Author l-f: 作楽ロク, 作楽ロク
My Review:
Volume 5
Chapter 25-30

This volume felt like it was broken into three parts, and each had a solid mix of humor, emotional development, and drama. I really liked how it was paced and started to pick up.

Introduction of Otsuka
I’m really glad we quickly established that Otsuka is a girl’s girl and genuinely kind. She could have easily been written as a typical rival, but instead, she adds warmth and support to the cast. This section also kicked off the whole romance misunderstanding arc. Plus, we got the slow burn of Sumire building a connection with Gotanda—which honestly might be a ship in the making. I wouldn’t hate it.

Field Day (within the School Festival arc)
Keisuke meddling in Yousuke and Tabata’s relationship? Hilarious. The fake sibling lie had me rolling, especially when Tabata called Yousuke “brother” and he nearly choked. Absolute gold. But the ending of that mini-arc really got me—Keisuke showing the “born in August” card? That was such a sweet and quiet emotional moment. Keisuke and Yousuke are still my favorites, with Gotanda close behind.

The School Festival
The sudden thunderstorm was classic shoujo drama and worked perfectly to bring Tabata and Yousuke closer. I really appreciated how the Field Day arc helped soften their awkwardness beforehand. Their chemistry was so cute during these chapters.
And finally—Yousuke’s feelings are slipping through. His jealousy is showing, and it’s clear he’s starting to see Tabata differently. He doesn't want to share her with others though he loves when others see her how he does too.. It's quite an adorable dilemma. The real surprise was Sumire. She dropped the act and confessed. That took guts, and I honestly respected her for it. Now it’s just a matter of time before Yousuke is forced to confront what he really wants.

Onto the next volume!

Title: ブスに花束を。(4) (角川コミックス・エース) (Japanese Edition)
Author: 作楽ロク
Author l-f: 作楽ロク, 作楽ロク
My Review:
Volume 4
Chapters 19-24

This volume had my heart.

For the first time, Tabata genuinely begins working on herself for herself, and it’s such a rewarding shift to witness. After volumes of insecurity and self-doubt, seeing her take steps toward growth and self-worth felt so earned in a way. I’m absolutely rooting for her now.

Keisuke, though? He stole the show. He’s officially the best wingman in the manga. The way he supports Tabata—not by coddling her, but by leading through example—is incredibly mature and wholesome. His interactions with her are full of sincerity, especially during the birthday shopping and gift-giving scenes. Those moments weren’t flashy, but they were practical and meaningful. Keisuke’s attitude in Chapter 23, his resolve about romance, and how he respects emotions even when they’re complicated—chef’s kiss. I love how he also got her online unlike the other kids. He took the steps to get her included and is slowly in his way including her into his and his family's lives.

Chapter 24, the fireworks/summer festival chapter, was beautifully done. It had all the emotional beats you’d want without being melodramatic. Keisuke coming to terms with his feelings for Tabata hit hard—even if it's only to his "middle school" friends.

But let’s talk about that one line… “Yousuke should’ve chosen someone cuter”? No. I don’t care if it was “just a joke”—that kind of comment is never harmless. It cut through the sincerity and made me wince. Even if it was meant to show middle/high school boy immaturity or peer pressure, it was a sour note. I'm glad Yousuke corrected his butt in a second flat and left the scene with Tabata. The new character introduction for the next volume has me a bit annoyed though. Tabata hasn't yet come to terms with much yet to be thrown yet another hurdle... but here's to growth and hope.

Still, this was easily the strongest volume so far. Emotional growth, character clarity, and just enough tension to keep things moving—this is the kind of development I’ve been waiting for.

Title: ブスに花束を。3
Author: 作楽 ロク
My Review:
Volume 3
Chapters 13- 18

Volume 3 opens with some sweet and surprisingly meaningful moments between Keisuke Ueno (Yousuke’s younger brother) and Tabata. I actually enjoyed getting a bit of his background and seeing how his personality contrasts with Yousuke’s. There’s something kind of charming about watching both brothers approach their crushes in their own sincere, awkward ways. Yousuke clearly likes Tabata, though I wouldn’t call it a full-blown “Love Love” just yet—more like “Like Love,” if that makes sense.

Meanwhile… I’m still just coping whenever Sumire and Shinbashi are on the page. Sumire continues to be grating, and I’ve officially accepted that she's just not a good person right now. Shinbashi, on the other hand, feels like a broken record—only now someone’s turned the volume up. This volume seems to be his time to shine (unfortunately), and while I get that he’s meant to stir things up, his presence feels more like a plot tool than genuine character growth. His purpose was clearly to spark some jealousy in Yousuke and get him to question Tabata’s closeness to other guys, but the whole setup felt a bit too forced for me.

Also, I’ll never fully get the teenage desperation to date just for the sake of having a boyfriend or girlfriend. That kind of drama always feels a little hollow to me, even if it’s common in these kinds of stories. I'm okay for the most part since FL/ML aren't the ones in desperation for a relationship... the others, though, are just too loud.

Still, I’m hanging in there. The subtle emotional developments between the leads keep me turning the page—I’m just hoping for a little more real movement soon.

Title: ブスに花束を。2
Author: 作楽ロク
Author l-f: 作楽ロク, 作楽ロク
My Review:
Volume 2
Chapters 7-12.5

I still don't like Sumire. Her two-faced behavior continues to grate on me—maybe her redemption arc is coming, but it definitely hasn't started yet. For now, she feels more like a plot device to frustrate than a character to empathize with.

Tabata, on the other hand, is drowning in her own self-doubt and pessimism. Her self-deprecating nature is becoming more painful than endearing, and it’s frustrating watching nothing get through to her. That said, her mom remains an unexpected highlight—easily the best "wing women" in the manga so far. Though it is awkward seeing a parent meddling in teen love, but somehow it works here, adding a layer of warmth and comedy.

Yousuke is painted as the classic dense male lead, but honestly, Tabata might be giving him a run for his money. They’re both trapped in their own heads, stuck overthinking and misunderstanding everything. Still, it’s clear that Yousuke sees Tabata differently from his other friends—even if he hasn’t realized it himself yet. Gotanda continues to be one of my favorite supporting characters—sharp, observant, and someone who clearly sees the tension between Yousuke and Tabata. It’s refreshing to have at least one person clued in and rooting for them.

I’m jumping into Volume 3 next, still holding out hope for a turning point. I need something to really hit both leads—and for it to stick. I'm in this for the long haul, but I need the emotional payoff to start soon.

Author: Jin Seo
My Review:
--review to come-- official finished the spinoff series 03/26/24!

So I really want to go back and rewrite all the chapter segments for every part of this webtoon, but this might take quite a while. Instead I'll write out my finally thoughts on this book.

The first two volumes were a lot of recap and waiting around for the main leads to start making any sort of progress. The third really started picking up the stakes of the story and what each character put on the line. Deaths needed to take place and trauma needed to occur. The author beautifully showed the depth of scars and the wounds they can inflict both persons. The whole things hurts to even think about as both characters wanted to love the other and because they never regretted that love it hurt them more to see that the other failed to meet expectation.

The two of them loved each other and further loved each other after meeting which is the reason for why they are in pain when they see the other. I wasn't even expecting a happy ending by the end of this series as they were stabbing each other with everything they had. They took away each other's reason to live and yet told the other they couldn't die. It was heart breaking and though it felt like i wanted to rush their healing process I'm eternally grateful to the author that they didn't.

The ending was satisfying. I couldn't see myself truly believing the two reached happiness with each other until the very last moments with everyone in the garden. It was a work of art a true masterpiece.

This will hold a place in my heart.

Author: Saha
My Review:
Alright so this is very cute at the start with what seems a clear path laid out for little Enisha. However, the cute Enisha being obsessed over her family quickly moves along as the plot of the story thickens.

People from her past life (from the same world just a different role as Great Mage) are haunting her mainly her closest companions as the Great Mage and her greatest enemy. The Two mages pestering her seemed understanding but they are off... They have complicated pasts that tied their lives to the Great Mage more personally than anything. It seems like a obsession issue since it's been a long time and the Great Mage position could have easily being handed over to another person but they refuse. Enisha's greatest enemy is doing a 180 with his objective solely focusing on marrying Enisha (though she's LITERALLY A CHILD). Again both sides are threatening her past as a means to control her powers as Great Mage (reincarnated). We have the added complication that we don't even know how or why Enisha had originally died and reincarnated into the 3rd star of the Hyperion Empire. Oh well, we'll get there someday.

It's not overly political but there are times that politics do move the plot along. I did enjoy Enisha bonding with her family and also making friends with main lead Cahil but there's not nearly enough of that as she grows up too quickly. I do like that there is not issue to succession in this family as the twin brothers get along better and better each time they are on screen (especially with help of Enisha). I don't like how Enisha can't be herself and must hide and manipulate situations that could endanger her identity of the Great Mage from the past. I just like the idea of a Girl boss Female lead kicking a** in a dress with magic and sword at hand with her loving family supporting her as she deals with all her past enemies with new insight, but it's not going that way. T_T


I'll get back to this when more seasons come along!

Title: 폭군을 길들이고 도망쳐버렸다 1 [Poggun-eul Gildeurigo Domangchyeobeoryeossda 1]
Author: Jihyun
My Review:
chapters 1-40 completed for this season!

This is a strange webtoon. So as a short plot summary it is about a girl who wanted nothing but the love of her family betrayed in the end. Charlize is the youngest daughter of a noble family and she was deeply hated and neglected because her birth caused the death of their mother. She grew up wanting to prove her worth and wanted love from those around her and unknowingly accepted the emperor's proposal to be his sword. Normally being someone's sword means to be their right hand man in war and guard etc (it's like being the imperial commander in a way but personally for the emperor). However, the emperor LITERALLY meant for Charlize to become a sword (a living breathing metal sword).

As you can expect this was not her dream... for generations the emperor and his follow predecessor all used Kiera (her sword name) to slaughter and kill whoever they pleased. Slowly she lost every bit of humanity in her as she begged for a chance to find revenge after 500 years of pain and torment.

And bam, the story starts at the beginning with Charlize still just a young child with plenty of time to seek and execute her revenge plan on the Empire's emperor as well as place a tyrant in his place to destroy the empire.

I was expecting a lot more detailed dethronement of the emperor and his slow death. I was EXTREMELY disappointed that it wasn't shown in more detail especially after emphasizing that this was Charlize's only wish. I wonder where this story will go now that the main conflict has resolved itself and all the smaller issues pertaining her family and past lover are pretty clear for Charlize. She doesn't hate or love any of them. She is indifferent to any of their existences so whatever they do doesn't matter to her one way or another. She should just spell it out to her tyrant whether she likes him or not and that's that also. It's not really that big of a deal now unless some random conflict arises this practically concluded the plot. I'm not sure if I will really continue this but I'll come back to it once completed.

My Review:

I enjoyed the plot and all of the smaller arcs that followed Tangning's rise to fame. It was highly addicting to listen to the audio as I walked to classes and during chores. It does get repetitive (which is why I'm letting go now) but the situations are always interesting. The way PR handles the issues pertaining to their artists isn't always perfect which is realistic to an extent. The imperfections are what allow the situations to repeat in a slightly different manner. Regardless, the main point is that this is a tale in which the rise to fame isn't sweet and simple, but filled with heartache. Tangning got the best form of support she could have ever needed through her husband. The two main characters are faithful to each other. They love each other and respect the other's wishes and support the other wholeheartedly. It's a lovely relationship, but I do wish ML did show more interest and parental love to his and Tangning's children. All in all, I feel the place I dropped the story is fine since it does finish the arc and does leave it off at the place where I can rest easy knowing the two main characters and all of the supporting characters are doing well and will live happy lives.

With so much going on like the Pharm Family conspiring against the Empire and causing an uprising... a lot could have happened, but it ended shortly. It wasn't as satisfying of an ending as I had honestly hoped but it somehow suits the main lead's personalities to just let it go. They have a new future to take care of now (I wish we got to see some kids though!!!!!)

Well, regardless of the ending I enjoyed the sweet read. It was a fun journey with both Caesar and Carnia. (I wish we could have gotten a bit more from the side characters!!! )

Title: 어느 날 공주가 되어버렸다 1 [Eoneu Nal Gongjuga Doeeobeoryeotda 1] (Who Made Me a Princess, Season 1)

Title: 버림 받은 황비 4 [Beorim Badeun Hwangbi 4]
Author: Ina
My Review:
Season 4, chapters 118-145, Abandoned Empress series completed.

I really like the start of the series. Aristia was headstrong in her determination to not love Prince Ruve, but at some point, her conviction to that statement became like an excuse for her to just hide. I really really hated her indecisiveness. She's make her decision and then be glad it wasn't followed through and then continue on making the same type of decisions over and over. Honestly, Jieun had a better resolve than Tia ever did. Jieun served her part well in this second life and I think she's much happier in this life now too.

It was an overall acceptable ending though it seemed very rushed the last 10 chapters. It touched up on all the major plot points and all the characters reaped what they had sown.

I respect Carsein's decision to hold back his feelings in order to just keep Tia close as a friend unlike Allendis crossing the line and literally disappearing from sight. I get that there shouldn't be happy endings for everyone but it doesn't feel like we really closed the chapter on Tia's potential lovers.
I really loved that Jieun revealed that she wanted to desperately change the past as well by getting revenge on those who put a sword through her and broke her heart. I couldn't stand her at first, but now I see she was also a victim of misunderstandings. Ruve never received love so he didn't know how to love. Jieun only ever received love but didn't know how to give back. Aristia only ever wanted to be loved and gave Ruve all of her love, but died without ever having it reciprocated.

It was surprising that Ruve actually started to miss Tia after he had killed her. So much so that he distanced himself from Jieun in a matter of 4 years. Part of the reasons why he had been so quick to anger and couldn't tolerate anything had been his misunderstandings and jealousy of Tia and poison. I wish we got more info on the details of this poison but hey it cleared up a lot. I lowkey wished we had snippets from the past that showed how both Ruve and Tia had been poisoned and slowly succumbed to their fates (through underhanded schemes). An overall tragic story with a redeemable ending. I loved it but it had to be docked down to 4 stars because of Tia's constant indecisiveness.
